measuredOn: the tree of the commit that removes the artifacts, against its parent
decision: The product owner instructed this clean up. Raw run artifacts - the TRX result files and the collected broker logs - leave the working tree; the compact JSON summaries, gate records, manifests and reports stay, because they are what an outbox record binds and what a reader reads. Nothing is deleted from history: the removal is an ordinary commit, so every removed file remains readable at its parent and its digest is manifested.
whyTheseAndNotOthers: A TRX is the raw output of one run. It is reproducible by rerunning, it repeats almost entirely between runs, and no outbox record binds one - that was measured, not assumed. The counters a record does cite are parsed out of it by tools/ci/run_test_category.py and written to the category JSON that stays.
retentionGoingForward: tools/ci/run_test_category.py writes the TRX to artifacts/run-output and only the category record to the evidence directory.
tools/ci/run_broker_category.py writes the collected broker log to artifacts/run-output.
/artifacts/ is ignored by .gitignore, and *.trx and evidence/**/*.log are ignored as a second line.

check_no_raw_run_artifacts_in_evidence in tools/ci/policy_validator.py fails the run when a TRX or a log reaches evidence/. Three cases in tools/ci/test_policy_validator.py hold it, one of which proves the rule leaves the category summary alone.
.github/workflows/build.yml uploads artifacts/run-output beside each category record, so a failed CI run still hands out its raw output without the repository carrying it.
notDecidedHere: Where raw artifacts are archived outside this repository, and for how long, is an infrastructure decision rather than a repository one. Nothing in this repository depends on an answer, because every removed file is still readable in git history.
